- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid mean reversion miss.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts early in the forecast window (days 1–5); apply a 1–3% downward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2), model often fails to adjust quickly; apply lagged correction: reduce forecast by 2–4% in next 2–3 days.
- When model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, consider mean reversion bias; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model tends to overreact; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high, not above 10% above prior peak.
